title: Algebraic manipulation
summary: Three moves tidy almost any algebra. You [[simplify|simplify]] by collecting [[like-terms|like terms]], [[expand|expand]] by multiplying out brackets, and [[factorise|factorise]] by putting brackets back in. Extended adds harder factorising and [[completing-the-square|completing the square]].

goals.text: Simplify an [[expression|expression]] by collecting like terms.
Expand a single bracket and a product of two brackets.
Factorise fully by taking out the [[highest-common-factor|highest common factor]].
Collect [[term|terms]] with powers and products, and expand two brackets with two letters or three brackets.
Factorise four terms in pairs, a [[difference-of-two-squares|difference of two squares]], a perfect square, quadratics and cubics with a common $x$.
Complete the square for any quadratic $ax^{2} + bx + c$.

before.prompt: What is the highest common factor of $18$ and $24$?
before.hint: List the [[factor|factors]] of $18$. Which is the largest that also divides $24$?
before.explain: $18 = 6 \times 3$ and $24 = 6 \times 4$, and $3$ and $4$ share no factor. $72$ is the lowest common multiple. Revise it in {{lesson:1.1}}.

before.hint: The coefficient includes the sign in front of the term.
before.explain: The term with $y$ is $-9y$, so the coefficient is $-9$. Revise it in {{lesson:2.1}}.

blocks.text: A [[term|term]] is one part of an [[expression|expression]], with the sign in front of it. In $4a - 3b + 6$ the terms are $4a$, $-3b$ and $6$.

blocks.statement: Terms with exactly the same letters, raised to the same powers. Only the number in front, the [[coefficient|coefficient]], can be different.
blocks.plain: $3x$ and $8x$ are like terms. $3x$ and $3y$ are not, and nor are $3x$ and $3x^{2}$.

blocks.text: To [[simplify|simplify]], add the coefficients of each group of [[like-terms|like terms]].
Keep each sign with the term after it. A letter on its own, like $q$, means $1q$.

blocks.question: Simplify $8m - 3 - 2m + 10 - m$.
steps: The $m$ terms, with their signs: $8m - 2m - m = 5m$.

blocks.text: Dropping a minus sign. $3b - 7b$ is $-4b$, not $4b$: you start at $3$ and go down $7$.

blocks.hint: Circle the $k$ terms and the $j$ terms, each with the sign in front of it.
blocks.explain: $9k - 2k = 7k$ and $-4j + j = -3j$. $11k$ comes from ignoring the minus in front of $2k$.

blocks.text: With powers and products, terms are alike only if they match exactly. $x^{2}$ and $x$ are not like terms. $yx$ and $xy$ are, because $yx = xy$. So $4x^{2} - 6xy - x^{2} + 8yx = 3x^{2} + 2xy$.

blocks.hint: Group the $a^{2}$ terms and the $ab$ terms. Collecting never changes a power.
blocks.explain: $a^{2} - 3a^{2} = -2a^{2}$ and $5ab - ab = 4ab$. The power stays $2$: you add coefficients, not powers.

blocks.text: To [[expand|expand]] a bracket, multiply every term inside it by the term outside. $4(x + 3)$ means four lots of $x + 3$, which is $4x + 12$.
When you multiply terms, multiply the numbers, then the letters. Add the powers of the same letter: $x \times x = x^{2}$ and $x \times x^{2} = x^{3}$.

blocks.question: Expand $6y(2y - 7)$.
steps: Multiply $6y$ by $2y$: $6 \times 2 = 12$ and $y \times y = y^{2}$, so $12y^{2}$.

blocks.text: A minus in front of a bracket multiplies every term inside. $-3(x - 6)$ is $-3x + 18$, because a negative times a negative is positive.

blocks.hint: The second bracket is multiplied by $-3$, not $3$.
Multiply both terms in the bracket by $-2a$. Watch the signs.
blocks.explain: $-2a \times a = -2a^{2}$ and $-2a \times (-9) = +18a$. $-2a^{2} - 9$ multiplies only the first term.

blocks.text: For two brackets, multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second. That gives four products. Then collect like terms.

blocks.alt: A two by two grid for expanding 2x minus 3 times x plus 6. The columns are headed x and plus 6, the rows 2x and minus 3. The four cells are 2x squared, 12x, minus 3x and minus 18.
blocks.caption: A grid keeps track of the four products in $(2x - 3)(x + 6)$.

blocks.question: Expand and simplify $(2x - 3)(x + 6)$.
steps: $2x$ times each term in the second bracket: $2x^{2}$ and $12x$.

blocks.text: The answer has an $x^{2}$ term and no higher power. That makes it a [[quadratic-expression|quadratic expression]].

blocks.hint: Do all four products. What is $-8 \times (-5)$?
blocks.explain: $x^{2} - 5x - 8x + 40 = x^{2} - 13x + 40$. Two negatives multiply to a positive, and $x^{2} + 40$ forgets the two middle products.

blocks.text: For three brackets, expand any two first. Then multiply each term of that answer by each term of the third bracket.

blocks.question: Expand and simplify $(x + 1)(x - 4)(3x + 2)$.
steps: Expand the first two: $x^{2} - 4x + x - 4 = x^{2} - 3x - 4$.

blocks.hint: Write $(x + 2)^{2}$ as $(x + 2)(x + 2)$ and expand that first.
blocks.explain: $(x + 2)^{2} = x^{2} + 4x + 4$. Times $(x - 1)$: $x^{3} - x^{2} + 4x^{2} - 4x + 4x - 4 = x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 4$. The second option squared only the $x$ and the $2$.

blocks.text: “Expand and simplify”: show all four products, then collect like terms. An answer left as four terms may lose the last mark.
To [[factorise|factorise]] is to undo expanding. You write the expression as a product: a [[common-factor|common factor]] outside a bracket.
Both terms of $8x + 20$ divide by $4$, a [[factor|factor]] of each. So $8x + 20 = 4(2x + 5)$. Expanding $4(2x + 5)$ gives back $8x + 20$.
“Factorise” means factorise fully. Take out the [[highest-common-factor|highest common factor]] (HCF), so the terms in the bracket share nothing more.
1. Find the HCF of the numbers.
2. Find each letter that is in every term, at its lowest power.
3. Divide each term by the HCF, write the results in the bracket, and expand to check.

blocks.question: Factorise $14m - 21$.
steps: The HCF of $14$ and $21$ is $7$. No letter is in both terms.

blocks.question: Factorise fully $18y^{2} - 12y$.
steps: Numbers: the HCF of $18$ and $12$ is $6$.
Letters: both terms contain $y$, and the lowest power is $y$. So the HCF is $6y$.
Check: $6y(3y - 2) = 18y^{2} - 12y$, and $3y$ and $-2$ share no factor.

blocks.text: Stopping too soon. $2y(9y - 6)$ is factorised, but not fully: $9y$ and $6$ still share $3$. Take out $6y$ in one go.

blocks.hint: Find the HCF of $15$ and $10$. Which letter is in both terms?
blocks.explain: The HCF is $5p$: $15p^{2} \div 5p = 3p$ and $10pq \div 5p = 2q$. The second and third options are true but not fully factorised.

blocks.hint: The lowest power of $x$ in both terms is $x^{2}$.
blocks.explain: The HCF is $4x^{2}$: $20x^{3} \div 4x^{2} = 5x$ and $8x^{2} \div 4x^{2} = 2$. The other two still have a common factor inside the bracket.

blocks.text: Here are five more patterns. Always take out any common factor first.
Four terms: group them in pairs that share a factor, and factorise each pair. If the two brackets match, take the bracket out.

blocks.question: Factorise $ab - 4b + 3a - 12$.
steps: Pair the first two and the last two: $b(a - 4) + 3(a - 4)$.
Both parts contain $(a - 4)$. Take it out: $(a - 4)(b + 3)$.

blocks.text: Difference of two squares: expand $(a + b)(a - b)$ and the $ab$ and $-ab$ cancel, leaving $a^{2} - b^{2}$. So one square minus another always factorises.

blocks.question: Factorise fully $50x^{2} - 8y^{2}$.
steps: $25x^{2} = (5x)^{2}$ and $4y^{2} = (2y)^{2}$, so the bracket is a [[difference-of-two-squares|difference of two squares]].

blocks.hint: Take out $3$ first. Is what is left a difference of two squares?
blocks.explain: $3k^{2} - 48 = 3(k^{2} - 16) = 3(k + 4)(k - 4)$. Stopping at $3(k^{2} - 16)$ is not fully factorised.

blocks.text: Quadratic $x^{2} + bx + c$: find two numbers that multiply to $c$ and add to $b$. If they are $p$ and $q$, the answer is $(x + p)(x + q)$. If no such whole numbers exist, it does not factorise into brackets with whole numbers.

blocks.question: Factorise $x^{2} - 2x - 24$.
steps: You need two numbers that multiply to $-24$ and add to $-2$.

blocks.text: Quadratic $ax^{2} + bx + c$ with $a \neq 1$: find two numbers that multiply to $ac$ and add to $b$. Use them to split the middle term, then factorise in pairs.

blocks.question: Factorise $3x^{2} + 10x - 8$.
steps: $ac = 3 \times (-8) = -24$. Two numbers that multiply to $-24$ and add to $10$: $12$ and $-2$.

blocks.hint: $ac = -24$. Which two numbers multiply to $-24$ and add to $5$?

blocks.text: Perfect square: $a^{2} + 2ab + b^{2} = (a + b)^{2}$ and $a^{2} - 2ab + b^{2} = (a - b)^{2}$. Spot it when the first and last terms are squares and the middle term is twice their product. The sign of the middle term goes in the bracket.

blocks.hint: Is $49$ a square? Is $14x$ twice $x$ times its square root?

blocks.text: Cubic $ax^{3} + bx^{2} + cx$: every term contains $x$. Take out $x$ (and any number factor), then factorise the quadratic left in the bracket.

blocks.hint: Take out $2x$ first, then factorise the quadratic left.

blocks.text: Stopping after the common factor. $2x(x^{2} - 9)$ is not fully factorised: $x^{2} - 9 = (x + 3)(x - 3)$.
[[completing-the-square|Completing the square]] writes a quadratic as a bracket squared plus a number, such as $(x - 3)^{2} + 5$. You use it to solve quadratics in {{lesson:2.5}}.
See how a square expands: $(x + 4)^{2} = x^{2} + 8x + 16$. The number in the bracket is half the coefficient of $x$. Squaring it adds $16$, which you must take away again.

blocks.question: Write $x^{2} - 10x + 7$ in the form $(x + p)^{2} + q$.
steps: Half of $-10$ is $-5$, so start with $(x - 5)^{2} = x^{2} - 10x + 25$.
That adds $25$ you don't want, so take it away: $x^{2} - 10x + 7 = (x - 5)^{2} - 25 + 7$.

blocks.text: When $a \neq 1$, take $a$ out of the $x^{2}$ and $x$ terms only. Complete the square inside the bracket, then multiply back.

blocks.question: Write $2x^{2} + 12x + 5$ in the form $a(x + p)^{2} + q$.
steps: Take $2$ out of the first two terms: $2(x^{2} + 6x) + 5$.

blocks.text: Forgetting to multiply the square you took away by $a$. In $2\big((x + 3)^{2} - 9\big)$, the $-9$ becomes $-18$.

blocks.prompt: Write $x^{2} + 8x - 3$ in the form $(x + p)^{2} + q$.
blocks.hint: Halve $8$. What does that bracket add when you square it?

blocks.prompt: Write $3x^{2} - 6x + 1$ in the form $a(x + p)^{2} + q$.
blocks.hint: Take $3$ out of the first two terms: $3(x^{2} - 2x) + 1$.

blocks.text: Like terms have the same letters and powers. Add their coefficients, keeping each sign.
Expand: multiply every term inside by every term outside. Two brackets give four products.
Factorise fully: take out the HCF of the numbers and the lowest power of each shared letter. Expand to check.
$ax^{2} + bx + c$: find two numbers that multiply to $ac$ and add to $b$. Split the middle term, then factorise in pairs.

mistakes: Stopping before factorising is complete. $3x(4x - 6)$ still has $2$ in common inside; take out $6x$ to get $6x(2x - 3)$.
Sign slips when multiplying: $-3 \times 4$ is $-12$, and $-3 \times (-4)$ is $+12$.
Losing a minus when collecting: $4b - 5b$ is $-b$, not $b$.
Multiplying the powers instead of adding them: $x \times x^{2}$ is $x^{3}$, not $x^{2}$.
Only multiplying the first term in a bracket: $5(x - 2)$ is $5x - 10$, not $5x - 2$.
examTips: “Factorise” and “factorise completely” both want the fully factorised answer. A partly factorised answer often earns only one of the marks.
“Expand and simplify”: write the products, then collect. If one term is wrong, the right ones can still earn a mark.
Expand your factorised answer back in your head. It takes seconds and catches sign slips.
